queue.question: Which current UE 5.8, SideFX Karma, and modern atmosphere/whole-atmosphere ideas are transferable into KAOPU as vendor-independent atmosphere/lighting semantics and evaluator contracts without copying engine implementations or defaults?
queue.progress: R01 separated atmosphere truth/state from evaluator policy using current UE 5.8, SideFX Karma, Hillaire 2020, Bruneton 2017, and Wilkie et al. 2021. R02 extended the candidate from lower-atmosphere rendering to continuous ground-to-space semantics using NASA layer references, current NASA CCMC NRLMSIS whole-atmosphere references, thermosphere/ionosphere model boundaries, and HITRAN-backed spectral semantics. R03 added executable evaluator evidence: one synthetic unit-explicit AtmosphereState was queried by spherical-reference and plane-parallel evaluators. The plane-parallel approximation was nearly exact for a vertical ground query but reached ~96% relative transmittance error at 89-degree view zenith, proving that evaluator authority must carry a measured validity envelope. R04 converted the Earth next gate into a multi-root reference suite rather than one blended profile: official U.S. Standard Atmosphere 1976 lower-atmosphere constants/equations were implemented and executed as a static regression root; official NASA CCMC NRLMSIS 2.1 remains a separate driver-conditioned root; packaged 500 km NRLMSIS test vectors transported through a non-authoritative mirror show a Candidate 338.21 K temperature span and ~7.72x total-density range across different context tuples at identical altitude, reinforcing that altitude alone is not a sample identity. R05 used current NASA CCMC plus the primary NRLMSIS 2.0/2.1 and 2025 SABER validation literature to separate measurement, retrieval, empirical-model output, holdout validation, external-sensor validation, and model-dependent retrievals. It found that evidence independence is multidimensional: different assets or sensors are not automatically independent if they share fit data, retrieval models, or upstream priors. The 2025 SABER NO retrieval uses NRLMSIS 2.1 temperature/O/O2 while adding full-local-time sensor information and exposes NO local-time structure not represented by current MSIS 2.1; therefore a provenance dependency DAG and per-variable coverage envelope are Candidate first-class semantics. R06 used current NASA CCMC, the primary 2022 NRLMSIS 2.1 model paper, and the official NRL release directory to separate global model domain from per-quantity validity and to refine validation-split independence. NASA accepts 0-1000 km model queries, while the primary paper says NO is missing below 72.5 km because of a fitted-profile edge artifact; therefore QuantityValidityEnvelope and typed Missing/Unsupported are Candidate first-class semantics. The same paper states the fitting/validation ensembles were sampled with repetition and observations may repeat across ensembles, so a holdout label does not guarantee sample disjointness. A semantic probe verified safe missing parsing and the overlap contract. Official NRL executable confirmation and authenticated HITRAN numeric checkpoints remain Unknown.
queue.nextGate: Execute selected NRLMSIS 2.1 cases from the authoritative NRL package or NASA CCMC and compare them against the Candidate release vectors. The locked fixture must record modelDomain separately from per-output QuantityValidityEnvelope, parse source-specific missing/unsupported values before transforms, and preserve EvidenceClass plus dependency/overlap metadata. Then retrieve a tiny authenticated HITRAN line subset and create two or three optical checkpoints with explicit molecule/isotopologue, spectroscopy provenance, temperature, pressure, line-shape model, path/column state, units, and tolerances. Candidate-complete promotion still requires authoritative NRL numerical confirmation plus authenticated spectral checkpoints; Frozen promotion remains a separate Judgment event.
